ch5-e1-spiral.caption: Phase portrait of $\dot x = -y + \lambda x(x^2+y^2)$, $\dot y = x + \lambda y(x^2+y^2)$ for $\lambda = -1$: trajectories wind counter-clockwise and spiral slowly into the origin.
ch5-e1-spiral.title: Nonlinear stable spiral (lambda = -1)

ch5-e10-quad-pendulum.caption: Exercise 5.10: pendulum with quadratic drag ($k = 0.4$). Although the linearization at $(2m\pi, 0)$ is a centre, $\dot E = -ky^2|y| \le 0$ forces orbits to spiral slowly into $(2m\pi, 0)$.
ch5-e10-quad-pendulum.title: Quadratically damped pendulum 5.10

ch5-e2-i.caption: Exercise 5.2 (i) for $x, y \ge 0$: dashed nullclines $y = 2 - x$ and $y = 1 - x$ do not intersect in the first quadrant; every interior orbit converges to $(2, 0)$.
ch5-e2-i.title: Competing species 5.2(i)

ch5-e2-ii.caption: Exercise 5.2 (ii) for $x, y \ge 0$: nullclines $y = 2 - x$ and $y = 1 - x/8$ cross at the stable coexistence node $D(8/7, 6/7)$, attracting all interior trajectories.
ch5-e2-ii.title: Competing species 5.2(ii)

ch5-e2-iii.caption: Exercise 5.2 (iii) for $x, y \ge 0$: the stable manifold (pink) of the saddle $D(2/7, 4/7)$ separates the basins of the two stable exclusion nodes $B(0, 1)$ and $C(2, 0)$.
ch5-e2-iii.title: Strong competition 5.2(iii)

ch5-e2-iv.caption: Exercise 5.2 (iv) for $x, y \ge 0$: closed counter-clockwise periodic orbits around the nonlinear centre $(2/3, 1/2)$, with saddle at the origin.
ch5-e2-iv.title: Lotka-Volterra predator-prey 5.2(iv)

ch5-e2-v.caption: Exercise 5.2 (v) for $x, y \ge 0$: saddles at $(0, 0)$ and $(8, 0)$; every interior orbit spirals counter-clockwise into the stable coexistence spiral $(2, 1)$.
ch5-e2-v.title: Logistic prey and predator 5.2(v)

ch5-e2-vi.caption: Exercise 5.2 (vi) for $x, y \ge 0$: unstable node $(0,0)$, saddles $(10,0)$ and $(0, 1/10)$, and stable coexistence spiral $(97/13, 11/13) \approx (7.46, 0.85)$.
ch5-e2-vi.title: Predator with alternative food 5.2(vi)

ch5-e2-vii.caption: Exercise 5.2 (vii) for $x, y \ge 0$: saddles at $(0, 0)$ and $(3, 0)$; all interior trajectories spiral into the stable coexistence spiral $(2, 1)$.
ch5-e2-vii.title: Logistic prey and predator 5.2(vii)

ch5-e3-i.caption: Exercise 5.3 (i) for $x, y \ge 0$: cooperation with finite carrying capacity; nullclines $y = x - 1$ and $y = (1 + x)/2$ intersect at the globally attracting stable node $(3, 2)$.
ch5-e3-i.title: Bounded cooperation 5.3(i)

ch5-e3-ii.caption: Exercise 5.3 (ii) for $x, y \ge 0$: nullclines $y = x - 2$ and $y = 4 + 2x$ diverge in the first quadrant; no interior equilibrium exists and both populations grow unboundedly.
ch5-e3-ii.title: Unbounded cooperation 5.3(ii)

ch5-e4-i.caption: Exercise 5.4 (i) with $\omega = 1$: concentric clockwise circles $y^2 + x^2 = 2E$ around the centre $(0, 0)$.
ch5-e4-i.title: Harmonic oscillator 5.4(i)

ch5-e4-ii.caption: Exercise 5.4 (ii): saddle at $(0, 0)$ with figure-eight homoclinic separatrix $E = 0$ (pink), centres at $(\pm 1, 0)$ for low-energy wells ($-1/2 < E < 0$), and high-energy orbits ($E > 0$).
ch5-e4-ii.title: Double-well oscillator 5.4(ii)

ch5-e4-iii.caption: Exercise 5.4 (iii) with the sheet potential $V(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}x^6 - \tfrac{5}{4}x^4 + 2x^2$: only $(0, 0)$ is a real equilibrium (centre), surrounded by nested clockwise periodic orbits.
ch5-e4-iii.title: Sextic single-well oscillator 5.4(iii)

ch5-e5-ii.caption: Exercise 5.5 (ii): bead moving on the wire $z = \tfrac{1}{2}x^4 - x^2$; same equilibria and figure-eight separatrix topology as Exercise 5.4 (ii), with flattened high-energy curves due to the $1 + (V')^2$ inertia factor.
ch5-e5-ii.title: Bead on a double-well wire 5.5(ii)

ch5-e6-i.caption: Exercise 5.6 (i) ($\omega = 1$, damping $-\dot x$): underdamped stable spiral at $(0, 0)$ with $\lambda = (-1 \pm i\sqrt{3})/2$.
ch5-e6-i.title: Damped harmonic oscillator 5.6(i)

ch5-e6-ii.caption: Exercise 5.6 (ii): the stable manifold (pink) of the saddle $(0, 0)$ partitions the phase plane into the basins of attraction of the two stable spirals $(-1, 0)$ and $(1, 0)$.
ch5-e6-ii.title: Damped double-well oscillator 5.6(ii)

ch5-e6-iii.caption: Exercise 5.6 (iii): with damping $-\dot x$, every orbit in the sheet potential spirals into the unique stable equilibrium $(0, 0)$.
ch5-e6-iii.title: Damped sextic oscillator 5.6(iii)

ch5-e8-pendulum.caption: Exercise 5.8: simple pendulum ($\omega = 1$). Centres at $(2m\pi, 0)$, saddles at $((2m+1)\pi, 0)$, separatrices $E = 1$ (pink) dividing librations ($|E| < 1$) from continuous rotations ($E > 1$).
ch5-e8-pendulum.title: Simple undamped pendulum 5.8

ch5-e9-damped-pendulum.caption: Exercise 5.9: damped pendulum ($k = 0.5 < 2$). Every trajectory not on a saddle stable manifold spirals into one of the downward equilibria $(2m\pi, 0)$.
ch5-e9-damped-pendulum.title: Damped pendulum 5.9 (k = 0.5)

ch6-e1-robin.caption: Exercise 6.1 (iv) ($h = 1$): intersections of $y = \tan\mu$ and $y = -\mu/h$ give the positive roots $\mu_n = \sqrt{\lambda_n} \in ((n-\tfrac{1}{2})\pi, n\pi)$, approaching $(n-\tfrac{1}{2})\pi$ from the right for large $n$.
ch6-e1-robin.title: Robin transcendental equation

ch6-e2-tan.caption: Exercise 6.2 (ii): intersections of $y = \tan\mu$ and $y = \mu$ yield the negative eigenvalues $\lambda_n = -\mu_n^2$ ($\mu_1 \approx 4.49$, $\mu_2 \approx 7.73$), in addition to $\lambda_0 = 0$.
ch6-e2-tan.title: Transcendental equation tan(mu) = mu

ch6-e5-step.caption: Exercise 6.5 (vii): $2\pi$-periodic extension of the step function on $[-3\pi, 3\pi]$ (blue) vs $S_{15}(x)$ (pink); green dots mark the jump midpoints $\pi/2$.
ch6-e5-step.title: Fourier series of step function 6.5(vii)

ch6-e8-i.caption: Exercise 6.8 (i) ($L = 1$): the $2L$-periodic extension of $f(x) = x^2$ is continuous everywhere (since $f(-L) = f(L) = L^2$), so $S_8(x)$ tracks it closely with no jumps.
ch6-e8-i.title: Fourier series of x^2 on [-L, L]

ch6-e8-ii.caption: Exercise 6.8 (ii) ($L = 1$): $2L$-periodic extension of $e^x$ (blue) vs $S_{12}(x)$ (pink); at every odd multiple of $L$ the series converges to the midpoint $\cosh L \approx 1.54$ (green dots).
ch6-e8-ii.title: Fourier series of e^x on [-L, L]

ch6-e8-iii.caption: Exercise 6.8 (iii) ($L = 1$): continuous at $x = 0$ (value $1$) with jumps at odd multiples of $L$ where the series converges to the midpoint $1 + L/2 = 1.5$ (green dots).
ch6-e8-iii.title: Fourier series of piecewise function 6.8(iii)
